title: Magnetic tuning of quantum backflow: Schrödinger vs Pauli system
abstract: Probability backflow is investigated for charged spin-$1/2$ particles in a uniform magnetic field within the lowest-Landau-level approximation. While single-mode Landau states exhibit only weak and non-robust backflow, it is shown that two-mode interference gives rise to negative probability flux in both the Schrödinger and Pauli formulations. In the Pauli case, orbital and spin contributions to the probability current are explicitly separated, revealing an additional interference mechanism. The external magnetic field is found to act as a tunable control parameter, simultaneously controlling the spatial overlap of orbitals and the spin dynamics. In the two-mode regime, a resonance between orbital mismatch and spin precession leads to an enhancement of backflow. Finite spatial resolution is shown not to suppress the effect within realistic coarse-graining. These results establish magnetic-field-controlled quantum backflow in Landau systems as an accessible interference phenomenon.
summary: This theoretical work examines quantum probability backflow in spin-1/2 particles in a magnetic field, contrasting Schrödinger and Pauli treatments. It shows that two-mode interference generates a measurable negative probability flux, which is tunable by the magnetic field. The key finding is that the spin dynamics introduce an additional, controllable interference mechanism essential for observing this effect.
main_problem: The paper investigates quantum probability backflow in charged spin-1/2 particles subjected to a uniform magnetic field, comparing results derived from the Schrödinger and Pauli formalisms.
main_result: Two-mode interference leads to observable negative probability flux (backflow) in both formulations, which is controllable by the external magnetic field, particularly showing enhancement at resonance between orbital mismatch and spin precession.
method: The analysis involves calculating the probability current using gauge-invariant forms (Schrödinger) and explicitly separating orbital and spin contributions (Pauli), followed by time integration to define a backflow functional.
model_or_system: The system models charged spin-1/2 particles confined to the lowest Landau level (LLL) in a uniform magnetic field. The theoretical framework compares the scalar Schrödinger equation with the spinor Pauli equation.
key_observables: Probability backflow (negative probability current), total longitudinal probability current (decomposed into orbital and spin parts), and the backflow functional $F(T)$.
important_parameters: The external magnetic field $B_0$ acts as the primary tunable control parameter. Key regimes include two-mode interference and resonance between spin precession and orbital mismatch.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the LLL approximation and assumes that finite spatial resolution does not suppress the backflow effect if the detector size is appropriately small compared to intrinsic scales.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dependence of the backflow functional on magnetic field strength ($B_0$) and spatial position ($x$), confirming the enhancement of negative probability flux under specific field conditions.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical framework by comparing Schrödinger and Pauli descriptions. It then analyzes single-mode behavior, followed by a detailed investigation of the two-mode regime where the interplay between spatial and spin dynamics is maximized.
why_interesting: The explicit separation of orbital and spin contributions in the Pauli formalism, coupled with the demonstration of magnetic field control over an interference phenomenon, provides a rich platform for studying spin-orbit coupling effects in condensed matter systems.
